scope: Theorem 11.3 (Global identification of the equality base) of the manuscript “The nonmaximal anti-de Sitter Penrose Inequality and original-data rigidity” (preprints/The-nonmaximal-anti-de-Sitter-Penrose-Inequality-and-original-data-rigidity-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9e2b9ba2768918dc), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 141. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The completed static base is globally isometric, including its smooth boundary and its normalized lapse, to h = dr2 FM (r) + r2 σ, λ = q FM (r), FM (r) = 1 + r2 − 2M r , r ≥ rh, (11.7) where the boundary is interpreted in spatial proper distance and M = rh + r3 h 2 = mAH > 0. (11.8) The boundary is the entire model horizon sphere, and the unique end corresponds to r → ∞.
